title: affine separated
explicit_hypotheses: f:X→S an affine morphism of schemes
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(f:X\to S\) be an affine morphism of schemes. Then \(f\) is separated and quasi-compact.

title: characterize affine
equivalent_conditions: S has an affine open cover W_j with f^{-1}(W_j) affine
X is isomorphic over S to relative Spec_S(A) for a quasi-coherent O_S-algebra A
additional_conclusions: When these hold, X is canonically Spec_S(f_* O_X)
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $f : X \to S$ be a morphism of schemes.
The following are equivalent
\begin{enumerate}
\item The morphism $f$ is affine.
\item There exists an affine open covering $S = \bigcup W_j$
such that each $f^{-1}(W_j)$ is affine.
\item There exists a quasi-coherent sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_S$-algebras
$\mathcal{A}$ and an isomorphism
$X \cong \underline{\Spec}_S(\mathcal{A})$
of schemes over $S$. 
\end{enumerate}
Moreover, in this case $X = \underline{\Spec}_S(f_*\mathcal{O}_X)$.

title: affine equivalence algebras
conclusions: Affine S-schemes contravariantly equivalent to quasi-coherent O_S-algebras via f↦f_*O_X

title: quasi coherence scalar restriction
conclusions: M quasi-coherent as O_S-module iff M quasi-coherent as A-module
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $S$ be a scheme and let $\mathcal{A}$ be a quasi-coherent
$\mathcal{O}_S$-algebra. An $\mathcal{A}$-module is
quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal{O}_S$-module if and only if
it is quasi-coherent as an $\mathcal{A}$-module.

title: affine equivalence modules
conclusions: Pushforward f_* gives equivalence of quasi-coherent O_X-modules with quasi-coherent A-modules
An A-module is quasi-coherent over O_S iff quasi-coherent over A

title: composition affine
explicit_hypotheses: X→Y→Z composable affine morphisms of schemes
standalone_statement_latex: For schemes \(X\xrightarrow{f}Y\xrightarrow{g}Z\), if \(f\) and \(g\) are affine, then \(g\circ f\) is affine.

title: base change affine
explicit_hypotheses: f:X→S an affine morphism of schemes
standalone_statement_latex: If \(f:X\to S\) is an affine morphism of schemes and \(S'\to S\) any morphism, then the base change \(X\times_S S'\to S'\) is affine.

title: closed immersion affine
explicit_hypotheses: i:Z→X a closed immersion of schemes
standalone_statement_latex: Every closed immersion \(i:Z\hookrightarrow X\) of schemes is an affine morphism.

title: affine s open
explicit_hypotheses: s a global section of L
conclusions: The natural inclusion X_s→X is affine
standalone_statement_latex: Let \(X\) be a scheme, \(\mathcal L\) an invertible \(\mathcal O_X\)-module, and \(s\in\Gamma(X,\mathcal L)\). If \(X_s\subseteq X\) is the nonvanishing locus of \(s\), then the inclusion \(X_s\hookrightarrow X\) is affine.

title: affine permanence
conclusions: If X→S affine and diagonal Y→Y×_S Y affine, then g affine
If X→S affine and Y→S separated, then g affine
Morphisms from affine schemes to schemes with affine diagonal are affine
Morphisms from affine schemes to separated schemes are affine
standalone_statement_latex:
Suppose $g : X \to Y$ is a morphism of schemes over $S$.
\begin{enumerate}
\item If $X$ is affine over $S$ and $\Delta : Y \to Y \times_S Y$ is affine,
then $g$ is affine.
\item If $X$ is affine over $S$ and $Y$ is separated over $S$,
then $g$ is affine.
\item A morphism from an affine scheme to a scheme with affine
diagonal is affine.
\item A morphism from an affine scheme to a separated scheme is affine.
\end{enumerate}

title: morphism affines affine
explicit_hypotheses: f:X→Y a morphism between affine schemes
standalone_statement_latex: Every morphism \(f:X\to Y\) of affine schemes is affine.

title: Artinian affine
standalone_statement_latex: For any scheme \(S\), Artinian ring \(A\), and scheme morphism \(f:\operatorname{Spec}(A)\to S\), the morphism \(f\) is affine.

title: get affine
explicit_hypotheses: j(Y)∩Z closed in Z (equivalently in X when contained in Z)
conclusions: In particular if X affine then Y affine
standalone_statement_latex:
Let $j : Y \to X$ be an immersion of schemes.
Assume there exists an open $U \subset X$ with complement
$Z = X \setminus U$ such that
\begin{enumerate}
\item $U \to X$ is affine,
\item $j^{-1}(U) \to U$ is affine, and
\item $j(Y) \cap Z$ is closed.
\end{enumerate}
Then $j$ is affine. In particular, if $X$ is affine, so is $Y$.
